note: Card withdrawn today. An interview outside school is arranged through the school or a family, in a public or supervised setting, recorded only with consent. goal: Inquiry: the method note and annotated bibliography drafted for the short project (the ELA project looked back on, or the stand-alone), and the interview or first-person report drafted as one paragraph (what I expected, what the person's experience showed, what changed)
note: The teacher writes feedback on the note, the bibliography and the report paragraph before the next session. Between sessions the host course carries the reading.

goal: Show-me: choosing a published form for an audience (a one-page brief, an infographic, a recorded talk, an exhibit), then the honesty review: the teacher thinks aloud through one quotation checked in its context, one source checked for fair representation and one disclosure line on an invented project with planted faults, and pairs find one more fault with the card
note: Opening retrieval: g10-label-own-work (a point-of-use credit). Minutes after the retrieval: about 12 for choosing a form (a sort of the four publishing format cards), about 20 for the honesty review model and the pair try. Using a machine-made text tool is never required; no claim that any tool is reliable or unreliable. `rights` read on the honesty review. ELA grade 11 unit 4 taught presenting before this unit; the day teaches choosing a form itself.

goal: Inquiry: the method note, bibliography and interview report revised from the feedback, and the published form made so it carries the line of reasoning and its evidence for its audience
note: Candidates kept: the 11-12 bold on the product carrying the line of reasoning and its evidence (no added time); the bold on judging one's product and process with self, teacher and peer feedback (the day 48 teacher feedback, a two-line peer comment today, about 4 minutes, and the day 52 self-check). The revised method note and bibliography are the IV.D.3 product.

goal: Inquiry: the honesty review run alone and without the card on one's own finished work, with fixes made privately
note: Opening retrieval: g10-lateral-machine-text (a disclosure line written for an invented tool use). Problems are fixed privately, never named before the class (APPROACH.md item 4).

goal: Inquiry: the work published to its audience, the revised interview or first-person report finalized and shared, and the self-check
note: The published work is scored as the VI.C.2 product (form, language and presentation for the named audience) and the interview or first-person report as the II.D.1 product, with the day 53 sitting. Published work uses initials or a class name.

goal: Grade 11 year-end check, unit 6's end-of-unit assessment: four unseen sources (a report, a data set, an interview, a machine-made text) cited in one full style; an unseen finished project reviewed for quotes out of context, missing credit, a missing disclosure line and one source summarized against its own conclusion; a published form chosen for a named audience with the reason; and, from unit 5, one fast-news capture on a new case
note: About 35 minutes, alone, no card. Also scored from unit 6's products: the revised method note and bibliography (days 48 and 50), the interview or first-person report (day 52, II.D.1) and the published work (day 52, VI.C.2). Week 31 of grade 11.

goal: Respond: the gaps retaught in groups by rubric step, one fresh try, and the grade 11 reflect step (the strongest step and one goal for grade 12)
note: Response time for check 6. Week 32 of grade 11: respond only.

goal: Show-me: the hook and the compelling question, then the teacher sets up a personal system (saved searches, a short list of sources checked laterally, a note system, the check-before-share habit) and runs it on an invented question
note: Opening retrieval (5 minutes, after the hook): g11-advanced-search (a saved search rerun). Card held by the teacher: "save it, check it, note it, pause before you share." Host: ELA grade 12 unit 1 reading and research routines (days 1 to 15, in step). Stand-alone: "Which training or program after school fits a goal you choose, and how do you check what its pages promise?"

goal: Practice: pairs holding the card build and run the system on a teacher question; then each student writes a private note from one of their strengths to one goal, and from that goal runs one search they choose on a next step after school, on the closed invented set of program pages
note: Practice of the day 55 system. Candidate kept (no added time): choosing materials by one's own interests and plans (11-12 bold) is the next-step search. The teacher sees only the search steps, never the strengths, the goal or the plan; no student is asked about family money or plans. Closed set only: the search runs on the unit 7 invented program pages, one of which makes promises that fail a lateral check (APPROACH.md, practice pages use invented sites). A student may repeat it on the real web at day 60 or at home, with the stop rule and the home note.

goal: Show-me: teaching one move (a lateral check, the stop rule or how to credit) to someone younger, with a short guide; the teacher models the guide and a teaching turn
note: Opening retrieval: g11-honesty-review (one honesty fault found). The stop rule is taught to younger children in its K to 2 words (close, tell, no blame). Copyright points stay general guidance, never legal advice.

goal: Inquiry: the guide drafted for a named younger learner
note: Card withdrawn today. The teacher writes feedback before the next session.

goal: Inquiry: the guide revised from the feedback, and the teaching rehearsed with a partner who plays an eager younger learner
note: The revised guide is part of the VI.D.3 product. The partner plays a cooperative learner only.

goal: Inquiry: the move taught to a younger class the teacher arranges, or to a family member at home, with a teaching record (the move shown, the learner's try, how the student clarified or corrected it); then the self-check
note: Candidate kept (no added time): a leadership role that helps others do their best work (11-12 bold) is the teaching itself. The record is observed by the teacher at school or written as a short account with no names on the home path; it is scored with the revised guide as the VI.D.3 product. Visits to younger classes are teacher-arranged.

goal: Grade 12 mid-year check, unit 7's end-of-unit assessment: the personal system run on an unseen question with a saved search, two checked sources and a note; a sample guide for younger students fixed for one unsafe step, one dishonest step and one use outside the law (an all-rights-reserved image reused without permission); and, from grade 11 on new cases, two citations in the full style and one honesty fault found
note: About 35 minutes, alone, no card. The revised guide (day 59) and the day 60 teaching record are scored together as the VI.D.3 product. Week 13 of grade 12, outside every grade 12 core check week.

goal: Respond: groups by the rubric step missed, a reteach for each, and one fresh try on a new case
note: Response time for check 7. Week 15 of grade 12 shares a week with a core check, which 9 to 12 allows. No readiness check before unit 8: its assumed rows were all used in grade 11.

goal: Show-me: the hook and the compelling question; the teacher chooses a capstone decision, maps the communities it touches (users, workers, neighbors, future users) and says where they stand among them and what follows
note: Opening retrieval (5 minutes, after the hook): g11-method-note, g11-publish-for-audience and g11-learn-across-difference (one line each on a given project). Card held by the teacher: "decision, evidence, who it touches, where I stand, checked by a peer." Where they stand is said about the topic, never about who they are; no student discloses identity, religion or family details. Candidate kept (no added time): corroborating across diverse sources and balancing perspectives (11-12 bold) begins in the communities map and is done in the day 66 audit. Host: ELA grade 12 unit 8 senior research (e12-research, weeks 25 to 32) and US History II unit 12 (us2-research-paper, weeks 30 to 32) are later than most of this unit; the unit runs the capstone on its own question, one question serves both where the teachers agree, and library adds no second paper. Optional host in step: ELA grade 12 unit 6, "Public words and a public decision" (e12-info-multiple-sources, weeks 18 to 21, beside days 64 and 65), a town zoning decision run under its own frame's guards and the evenness rule. Stand-alone: "How should our school spend a one-time grant for student spaces?"

goal: Inquiry: in the first 10 minutes, after the card is withdrawn, each student names their capstone decision and drafts their own communities map; then search rounds and the log on that question, run on the student's own personal system
note: Card withdrawn today. The decision and the map are the student's own (the day 63 show-me is the model); where the student stands is said about the topic, never about who they are. The problem is chosen evenly across views; no partisan stand is required. Open search only on a teacher-guided inquiry day, pairs at one shared device at most, with the stop rule (close the page, tell the adult, no blame); the teacher page says what the adult does if an unsafe result appears and points to health's steps if a student tells something worrying; the student page says "your search results" and names no site. Paper path: the closed invented set.

goal: Inquiry: the recommendation drafted with its evidence, one competing interpretation answered, the "where I stand and what follows" paragraph written from the day 64 communities map, and the method note and annotated bibliography
note: Candidate kept (about 5 minutes of the draft): a line of argument that takes in or answers a competing interpretation with credible evidence (11-12 bold). The teacher writes feedback before day 67.

goal: Practice: the lateral audit of a classmate's capstone source list, each source checked laterally, two claims traced upstream and the citations checked, written as feedback on the audit sheet
note: Opening retrieval: g11-lateral-news (one update checked). Practice of the band's lateral, tracing and citation moves (units 1, 4, 5, 6) on a new list. The audit is taught without shaming: a weak source is fixed, never named before the class.

goal: Inquiry: one's own capstone fixed from the audit received and the teacher's written feedback, the communities map and the "where I stand" paragraph included
note: Fixes are private.

goal: Inquiry: the published form made for the people the decision affects, in a form grade 11 practiced
note: Published work uses initials or a class name. A student 18 or over gives their own consent for any interview used.

goal: Inquiry: the capstone published and shared with its audience, its communities map and "where I stand and what follows" paragraph in the published form, and the self-check
note: Self-check: the card's steps rated, one thing to do differently. Week 29 of grade 12.

goal: End-of-unit assessment: the capstone scored on its rubric, with a short sitting on the student's own capstone (an unseen source audited, and where they stand and what follows)
note: Inside the unit, week 29, so the score stands if seniors leave before week 31 (frame, Grade 12 calendar). Sitting about 20 minutes, alone, no card; it traces no claim upstream (the capstone carries its own traces from the day 66 audit, and check 8 nine school days later uses that form); the capstone is scored from days 65 to 69. Results go to each student in writing; day 72 returns them if it runs.

goal: Grade 12 year-end check, the band's last: three compact unseen cases (a source checked laterally with one claim traced upstream, on a street-trees or night-sky page from unit 1's or unit 4's content; a short set of three half-page sources, its two views stated fairly and one connection mapped; one flawed citation and one misread license label corrected)
skills: g9-lateral-method; g12-lateral-capstone; g9-fair-sides; g10-synthesis-map; g11-method-note; g9-open-licenses
note: About 35 minutes (12, 14 and 9), alone, no card. Case 1 is labeled "units 1 and 4": it samples unit 8's audit move on earlier units' content, so it repeats no day 70 item. Unit 7's system and unit 8's capstone are already scored and reused, not retaken. Week 31 of grade 12. Folds if seniors leave before week 31 (Shorter path).

goal: Respond: each student's results returned with written feedback, and the band's reflect step on the four years
note: Response time for check 8 and the capstone. Week 32 of grade 12: respond only. Folds if seniors leave before week 31: feedback on the capstone goes to each student in writing.
